main_text.p: autem dicit: Gloriam meam{1}, alteri non dabo, & laudem meam sculptilibus. Unde, quia sculptam sui imaginem Deum vocat ipse, vetans{b} Deos aureos argenteosve fieri: restat simulacrum imaginemque Dei, ex Scripturae phrasi: Deum esse alium. Porro quicunque Deum alium colunt, contra mandatum, {c}Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & eum solum coles; ii{d} Deum derelinquunt & irritum faciunt foedus eius: similiter atque adultera, ad alterum se conferens, & {e}eum benevolentia, quam marito soli debet, complectens, {f}derelinquit maritum suum, & conjugale foedus violat. Etiamne sui mariti imaginem in altero illo habeat, & amplectatur? Etiam. Et quidem tanto magis interdum, quanto clarioris imaginis in amplexus ruit. Filius, quem homo naturaliter {g}gignit ad similitudinem suam, est imago patris: eoque expressior, quo illustrius patrem undequaque refert; ut Caecinae filius, quem {h}Cicero imaginem animi & corporis patris sui vocat. Talis imago Thesei fuit Hippolytus: cujus impudico amore capta Phaedra noverca, conjux Thesei, sciebat, conjugale foedus suo scelere violatum iri. Nihilominus Thesei imaginem in illo videbat & deperibat: sicut apud {i}Tragicum (qui rem, ut verisimiliter accidere potuit, fingit) Hippolyto dicenti, Amore nempe Thesei casto furis; respondens introducitur,

p.i: Hippolyte sic est: Thesei vultus amo Illos priores quos tulit quondam puer, Quum prima puras barba signaret genas, Monstrique caecam Cnosii vidit domum, Et longa curva fila collegit via. Quis tum ille fulsit? praeferant vitta comam:

page.notes: Marginal notes in the right margin, placed at their reference marks in the text: {1} "1 Heb." followed by Hebrew, which I could not read reliably; {b} "Exod.10.2[?]"; {c} "Matt. 4.10."; {d} "Deut. 31.16. & 32.15."; {e} "Prov.7.18."; {f} "Prov.2.17."; {g} "Gen.5.3."; {h} "Epist.ad fam.li.6.ep.6."; {i} "Senec. in Hippolyto." Also note {a}, "Efai.42.8.", which stands beside the first line and is not placed in the text above. Note "2" beside the text reads "Adulter & adultera dicitur, quia ad alteram se conferens..." with the rest of its line illegible in the scan. Notes beside "Festus." and "Peius adulterio turpis adulter obest" and "Phaedra Hippolyto" and "Ovid. Heroid. epist. 4." are small and partly illegible. Hebrew in note 1 is marked illegible. Long s has been transcribed as s throughout, so "sic est" and "fulsit" are my readings of "fic eft" and "fulfit". Line "Quis tum ille fulsit?" is doubtful.
